This page was rendered with the [quarto-webmcp](https://github.com/alexanderwiebe/quarto-webmcp) extension.
In a browser with WebMCP, an agent can call the page's tools to read it.

## Try it

Any browser will do. Open the developer console and run:

```js
window.siteTools.list().map(t => t.name)
JSON.parse(await window.siteTools.call('get_post_claims', {}))
```

`<html data-webmcp>` shows whether the tools were registered with WebMCP (`registered`), or the browser doesn't support it (`unavailable`).

## How it works

The `webmcp` filter embeds the page's metadata and outline as JSON and attaches a small script.
The script reads that JSON and the rendered content, and registers the tools with `document.modelContext`.

## In a website

Put `filters: [webmcp]` and the `webmcp:` settings in `_quarto.yml`, and add the post-render script:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  post-render: _extensions/alexanderwiebe/webmcp/webmcp-index.ts

filters:
  - webmcp
```

The site then also gets `list_pages`, `get_page`, `list_posts`, `get_post` and `search_site`, which read the `webmcp-index.json` the script writes.
